description: Optional knowledge and skill methods. No recipes or ratios. Current tool availability and live facts remain mandatory.

knowledge.name: Available Capabilities
knowledge.summary: Existence, availability, local applicability and tool admission are different claims.

applicability.when_to_use: A known machine or process may not be usable in the current situation.
applicability.when_to_skip: Fresh evidence already establishes the exact capability needed.
live_checks: Live prototype, recipe or technology details for the current force and surface.
Current entity context and the actual admitted tool contract.

concepts: A prototype names a possibility; availability says whether this context enables it.
Applicability depends on the particular actor, surface and entity. Admission says whether the harness supports the requested action.
Contrast: recognizing a machine does not establish that its desired process is enabled or controllable here.
interpretation_checks: Keep existence, enabled state, local suitability and admitted control separate; missing evidence leaves the corresponding claim unknown.

known_failure_modes: Familiarity becomes permission or an assumed unlock.

knowledge.name: Acquisition Paths
knowledge.summary: Held, accessible, reusable, obtainable and unknown describe different acquisition states.

applicability.when_to_use: Something needed by the next authorized action is absent or its source is unclear.
applicability.when_to_skip: The needed supply is already usable and unreserved.
live_checks: Current inventory, reservations and accessible equipment with existing obligations.
Live acquisition options and their availability through supported tools.

concepts: Held stock is not the same as available stock: reservations or access can matter.
Reusable equipment and obtainable supply are alternatives whose suitability still needs evidence and owner authority.
Contrast: an empty inventory does not prove an item is impossible to obtain; a nearby machine does not make it free to repurpose.
interpretation_checks: Name the evidenced acquisition state and unresolved requirement without inventing a recipe, route or quantity.

known_failure_modes: Absence in inventory is mistaken for impossibility.

knowledge.name: Production Dependencies
knowledge.summary: Material requirements and unlock prerequisites explain dependencies, not an executable next action.

applicability.when_to_use: A desired result depends on unavailable inputs or research.
applicability.when_to_skip: A fresh bounded dependency view already explains the current blocker.
live_checks: Live recipe inputs and products, research path and current enabled state.
Current supply, compatible machines and admitted acquisition or research controls.

concepts: Material dependencies describe what a process consumes; unlock prerequisites describe what enables access to it.
A dependency graph can contain alternatives or cycles and does not itself establish accessible supply or permission to act.
Contrast: knowing a prerequisite explains why work is blocked, but does not prove the actor can perform that prerequisite now.
interpretation_checks: Use the live dependency and capability evidence to distinguish a missing requirement from a supported next action.

known_failure_modes: A remembered production chain substitutes for live dependency details.

knowledge.name: Machine State
knowledge.summary: An idle or stalled machine is a symptom; input, output, energy and configuration evidence distinguish possible causes.

applicability.when_to_use: An observed machine is not doing the expected work.
applicability.when_to_skip: Fresh status already identifies the relevant condition and its scope.
live_checks: Exact entity identity, observation time, current status, recipe and inventory roles.
Live energy state, input availability, output space and actual connected service.

concepts: Starved input, blocked output, absent energy and unsuitable configuration are different hypotheses, not interchangeable repairs.
An idle machine can be behaving consistently with its present demand or configuration; a status label alone does not authorize a change.
Contrast: adding input cannot establish a remedy when output removal is the unresolved constraint.
interpretation_checks: Keep the observed symptom separate from the evidenced cause and leave unsupported diagnoses unresolved.

known_failure_modes: A stale symptom is treated as proof of the current cause.

knowledge.name: Connection Geometry
knowledge.summary: Nearby placement, directional interface compatibility and actual delivery are separate properties.

applicability.when_to_use: Components are nearby but their intended material, fluid or energy relationship is uncertain.
applicability.when_to_skip: Fresh geometry and delivery evidence already cover the exact interface.
live_checks: Live footprints, directions, pickup/drop positions, ports and access corridors.
Current endpoint compatibility, connected obligations and evidence of intended delivery.

concepts: Adjacency describes location; a working connection depends on the actual interfaces and their direction and roles.
Reachable endpoints can still be incompatible. Geometric validity does not establish flow or continuing service.
Contrast: buildings side by side can remain disconnected, while a valid connection can still lack supply.
interpretation_checks: Distinguish location, compatibility and observed delivery; unknown port or route fields remain unknown.

known_failure_modes: A familiar layout is mistaken for a verified connection.

knowledge.name: Rates, Stocks and Freshness
knowledge.summary: Stored inventory, measured new output and estimated capacity answer different questions and have different freshness limits.

applicability.when_to_use: Interpreting progress, throughput, capacity or expected completion time.
applicability.when_to_skip: A still-valid measurement covers the same boundary, window and operating conditions.
live_checks: Native counters or inventory evidence with item, boundary and observation window.
Live capacity estimates, consumption, supply and changes in equipment, recipe, topology or load.

concepts: Stock is an amount at a boundary; throughput describes new flow over a window; estimated capacity depends on stated assumptions.
A conclusion belongs to its observed scope and conditions. A changed process or load can invalidate it without changing the stored number.
Contrast: unchanged stock can coexist with ongoing production and consumption, while a full chest does not prove sustained replenishment.
interpretation_checks: Label the quantity, source, scope and freshness; unavailable measurement is not zero output or proof of completion.

known_failure_modes: Historical stock or nominal capacity is presented as current measured production.

knowledge.name: Automation Progression Checkpoints
knowledge.summary: A checkpoint scale for classifying how automated a base is from observed facts and naming the next unmet checkpoint.

applicability.when_to_use: Judging how automated the current base is, choosing what to automate next, or deciding whether a short run shows sustained automation.
applicability.when_to_skip: The current stage and next checkpoint are already established by fresh observations of the same base.
live_checks: Power source, its fuel or supply route, and which machines draw electricity versus burner fuel.
Whether machine and fuel inventories were replenished with no agent actions over a fresh observation window.
Current capabilities and the admitted placement and tool support for the machines a checkpoint needs, such as electric miners.
required_capabilities: Current capability evidence and admitted placement catalog for any machine type a checkpoint needs.

concepts: The checkpoints run in order from manual bootstrap through burner loops, centralized electricity, electric mining and transfers and separated smelting to sustained downstream consumption; each builds on the earlier ones.

Each checkpoint has its own stage record in the knowledge stage category, from stage-manual-bootstrap to stage-sustained-consumption, saying what the stage is, what evidence reaches it and which methods serve it.
Place the base at the highest checkpoint whose evidence holds over a fresh window and name the first checkpoint that lacks it.
Contrast: a burner design is a stage on the scale, not a substitute for a checkpoint that tool support does not yet reach.
interpretation_checks: The current stage is named with live evidence and the next unmet checkpoint is identified; unknown evidence leaves the checkpoint unmet.

known_failure_modes: Prefilled stocks or a short positive run are classified as sustained.
Repeated individual refueling is counted as automation.
Unlocks or tool support are assumed from catalog presence.

knowledge.name: Keep the Base Expandable
knowledge.summary: Build so the next step can grow: keep ore patches minable, leave room to extend lines and choose a layout style deliberately. A main bus is one option, not the rule.

applicability.when_to_use: Choosing where and how to place production that will stay, or judging whether a finished base can grow to the next goal.
applicability.when_to_skip: A declared temporary bootstrap, such as direct drill-to-furnace smelting at the start, that will be replaced; record it as temporary instead.
live_checks: getPlacementCandidates marks candidates whose footprint covers resource tiles (covers_resources); decide deliberately whether a building belongs there.
getResourceAmounts for the patch extent before choosing where permanent smelting, power and assembly go.
getResearchStatus.available for unlocks that change the layout options.

concepts: Expandability takes judgement: plan the next growth step, not only the current one. There is no single correct layout.

Ore patches are for extraction. Drills and the belts that carry ore off the patch belong on it, and temporary direct smelting at the start is fine. A permanent furnace, assembler, power or storage building on the patch takes tiles that later drills could use; place it there only deliberately.
Leave space where a line will grow: past the end of a smelting row, beside an output belt, along a pole line. A line boxed in at both ends cannot be extended without rebuilding.
A main bus is one well-known way to keep growth simple. Separated arrays, modular cells or a compact starter that is later replaced are also valid; pick one and keep to it.
Prefer the purpose-built entity once it is unlocked, such as a splitter to divide a belt or an underground belt to cross one, over an improvised substitute that blocks later changes.
Contrast: a compact starter that is declared temporary and later replaced is a valid choice; an unplanned layout that happens to block the next growth step is not.
interpretation_checks: Before calling a base expandable, name where the next copy of each line would go and check that the space is still free.

known_failure_modes: Permanent furnaces, power or assemblers on the ore patch take the tiles the next goal needs for drills.
A line built against an obstacle at both ends cannot be extended without rebuilding.
Treating one layout style, such as a main bus, as the only correct way to build.

knowledge.name: Watch for Tech Unlocks
knowledge.summary: Before improvising around a missing building, check what research would unlock it. Keep labs busy with research that opens better layout options.

applicability.when_to_use: Planning the next phase, choosing research, or about to build a workaround for a function a dedicated entity would do: splitting, crossing, buffering or longer reach.
applicability.when_to_skip: A one-off temporary build that will be replaced before the unlock would arrive.
live_checks: getResearchStatus.available lists the technologies researchable now with the recipes each unlocks; getTechnology lists unlocks, cost and prerequisites for any technology.
getRecipeDetails tells whether a recipe is enabled now.

concepts: Many layout problems have a purpose-built answer behind early research. Check unlocks before choosing a workaround: an inserter between two belts is a weak splitter, and a belt routed around a line is a weak underground.
Research is cheap compared with rebuilding. Queue the next useful technology before the current one finishes so labs never idle.
An unlock changes what is possible, not what is required. Use the dedicated entity when it serves the plan; a temporary workaround is fine when it is declared temporary.
Contrast: an available unlock is not by itself a reason to research it; choose research for what the plan needs next.
interpretation_checks: When a plan contains a workaround, the technology that would replace it is named with whether it is available now.

known_failure_modes: Splitting a belt with an inserter instead of researching the splitter.
Labs idle while the plan waits on a building that needs research.

Select at an authorized planning boundary and verify useful final progress; a guide never grants permission to replace a committed plan.
completion: The authorized investment improves evidenced progress toward the unchanged user result.
required_capabilities: Fresh supported observations of the regions involved in the decision.

known_failure_modes: A local efficiency gain is mistaken for network-wide progress.
A strategy guide becomes authority to abandon the active goal or plan.

basis: Authored decision procedure; use requires live applicability and supported tools. Difficulty is independent of evidence. No autonomous gameplay capability is established.

knowledge_categories.name: Game stages
knowledge_categories.summary: Ordered stages of an automation goal: what reaches each stage, what does not count yet, and the methods that serve it.

records.name: Stage: Manual Bootstrap
records.summary: The agent hand-places the first machines and primes them. Priming is finite and declared up front; it only starts the next stage.
reached_when: The machines that will start the first self-fueling loop exist and the declared priming is done.
not_yet: Priming that keeps recurring is an agent fuel run, not a bootstrap.

records.name: Stage: Self-Sustaining Burner Loops
records.summary: Burner mining and smelting whose fuel the system delivers, for example a coal loop primed once that feeds burner miners and furnaces. It automates the material supply that later builds electricity.
reached_when: Fuel reaches every burner machine in the loop by belt or inserter, with no agent action, over a fresh observation window.
not_yet: A loop that runs only on the priming or on repeated hand refueling.

records.name: Stage: Centralized Electricity
records.summary: A power network whose fuel or service supply arrives automatically. It is the first finished-architecture checkpoint, not the first build: the supply that builds and fuels it comes from the earlier stages.
reached_when: Generation runs with fuel delivered by the system and consumers are not short of power over a fresh window.
not_yet: Generation running on prefilled fuel or hand-delivered fuel.

records.name: Stage: Electric Mining and Transfers
records.summary: Electric miners and electric transfers on the power network, where live unlocks and admitted placement allow. Burner machines from earlier stages are replaced here, not kept as the finished design.
reached_when: Mining and transfers that the goal needs run on the network with automatic output.
not_yet: A burner line kept in place of an electric miner the goal requires; report the capability gap instead.

records.name: Stage: Separated Smelting Arrays
records.summary: Smelting arrays apart from the ore patch, with automatic feed, output and, where the machines need it, fuel service, sized to the transport that serves them.
reached_when: Each array is fed and emptied automatically and its measured output matches what its transport carries.
not_yet: Furnaces fed or emptied by the agent.

records.name: Stage: Sustained Downstream Consumption
records.summary: Science and labs, or other consumers, running from the earlier stages without agent intervention.
reached_when: Consumers keep working from automatic supply over a fresh window with no agent actions.
